title: Detecting Errors in Large Language Model Responses: The Incremental Predictive Value of Hidden States
abstract: arXiv:2610.27455v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Although large language models support a wide range of tasks, hallucinations remain a major obstacle to user trust. When a model generates an answer, both its internal processing and final output vary with the question. Internal states are often expected to offer richer signals for hallucination detection. However, studies using these states typically report their standalone discrimination performance, while output-side comparisons often use simple baselines with weaker modeling capacity. We integrate output-side information available at inference time into a combined baseline and compare detection performance before and after adding hidden states under identical data splits and evaluation rules. Experiments cover open-ended generation and constrained multiple-choice tasks across different models. translated_title: 检测大语言模型回答中的错误：隐藏状态的增量预测价值
translated_abstract: 尽管大语言模型能够支持广泛的任务，但幻觉问题仍是阻碍用户信任的主要障碍。当模型生成回答时，其内部处理过程和最终输出都会随问题而变化。人们通常期望内部状态能为幻觉检测提供更丰富的信号。然而，使用内部状态的研究通常只报告其单独的判别性能，而输出侧的对比往往采用建模能力较弱的简单基线。我们将推理时可获得的输出侧信息整合为一个综合基线，并在相同的数据划分和评估规则下，比较添加隐藏状态前后的检测性能。实验涵盖了不同模型上的开放式生成任务和受限的多项选择任务。结果显示，添加隐藏状态使两项任务的AUROC分别仅提升约0.004和0.039。因此，隐藏状态能够提供的是额外的预测价值。
tldr: 该论文通过将输出侧信息整合为强基线并在公平条件下对比，发现隐藏状态对大语言模型错误检测的增量预测价值十分有限（AUROC仅提升约0.004至0.039）。
en_tdlr: Under fair comparisons against a strong output-side baseline, hidden states provide only marginal incremental predictive value for detecting LLM errors, improving AUROC by merely ~0.004–0.039 across tasks.
